protocol.name: zspatial_toplevel_export_v1
protocol.description:
This protocol lets a producer compositor delegate individual toplevel windows — the client's own buffer stream, the full surface tree, and an input back-path — to a consumer compositor, which presents them as first-class windows of its own scene. It is presentation-grade delegation, not screen capture: buffers are the client's original allocations, presentation is paced by the consumer, and the producer retains all shell authority over its clients (serials, grabs, popup placement, activation).
The consumer is an ordinary, privileged Wayland client of the producer. The zspatial_toplevel_export_manager_v1 global must only be exposed to authorized connections (compositor policy: a trusted dedicated connection, security-context based filtering, or an equivalent authorization mechanism). Toplevel enumeration through ext-foreign-toplevel-list grants neither export nor input authority, and the producer may deny or revoke the delegation of any surface at any time.
While a toplevel is delegated, the producer ceases presenting it locally and delivers no input to it from its own devices; the local window- management state of a delegated toplevel is specified by the producer conformance rules accompanying this protocol, not by wire messages.
File descriptors are owned by the receiver: plane, timeline, and keymap fds transferred by events or requests are duplicates the receiving side must close. Unless otherwise specified, timestamps are in the producer's CLOCK_MONOTONIC domain, with millisecond timestamps following wl_pointer semantics. Where 64-bit values are carried as two arguments, the value is 'hi' * 0x100000000 + 'lo'.
Colour-management and colour-representation state is not carried in version 1 of this protocol: consumers must treat exported content as sRGB, and producers must not deliver buffers whose committed colour state differs from the producer's default interpretation — such nodes take the color_state fallback instead. A capability bit is reserved for a future colour-carrying version.
The key words "must", "must not", "required", "shall", "shall not", "should", "should not", "recommended", "may", and "optional" in this document are to be interpreted as described in IETF RFC 2119.
Warning! The protocol described in this file is currently in the experimental phase. Backward incompatible changes may be added without bumping the major version of the extension. As such, gating usage on the protocol's presence is discouraged outside Mura itself.

interface.name: zspatial_toplevel_export_manager_v1
interface.description: The privileged entry point advertised by the producer. The capabilities event tells the consumer which optional protocol features this producer implements; requests that depend on an absent capability are ignored, and objects that depend on one become inert or are denied as specified per request.

entry.name: already_exported
entry.summary: the toplevel already has an exported tree on this connection

enum.name: capability
enum.description: Optional features of this producer. dmabuf: nodes deliver the client's own dmabuf allocations. input: get_input is honored. pacing: get_pacing is honored. detach_drag: mid-move handoff is honored. dnd: cross-export drag-and-drop (no producer is expected to set this in version 1). color: reserved for a future colour-carrying version; producers must not set it in version 1.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the manager object. Existing exported trees and their child objects are not affected.

request.name: export_toplevel
request.description: Request export of the toplevel identified by the given ext_foreign_toplevel_handle_v1; identity is always the handle, never title or app-id matching. The producer answers on the returned tree with either node announcements or a denied event. Requesting a second tree for the same toplevel on the same connection raises the already_exported error. If the handle is inert, the returned tree receives denied with the gone reason.

request.name: detach_drag
request.description: Request delegation of the toplevel currently held in the producer's interactive move on the given seat, identified by the producer's active move-grab. The producer ends its move with no placement side-effects (no electric borders, tiling, or output snap) and announces the export on the returned tree, beginning with an anchor event carrying the surface-local cursor-anchor point, so that the consumer's grab can keep the same content pixel under its cursor or ray. If no interactive move is active on the seat when the request is processed — including the race where the move ended in flight — the tree receives denied with the no_active_move reason. Without the detach_drag capability the tree receives denied with the unsupported reason.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: the producer seat whose move-grab is taken over

event.name: capabilities
event.description: The producer's capabilities. Sent on bind, before any other event on this object, and again whenever the set changes. Losing a capability revokes objects that depend on it: affected trees receive denied with the unsupported reason.

event.name: main_device
event.description: The DRM device (dev_t, native endianness) client buffers are expected to be allocated on, so the consumer can verify import compatibility before requesting an export. Sent once on bind, after capabilities, and again if the device changes; a change invalidates no existing tree, but subsequent buffers may arrive with a different device.

arg.name: device
arg.summary: dev_t of the producer's main device

interface.name: zspatial_exported_tree_v1

description.summary: one delegated toplevel and its surface tree

interface.description:
One exported toplevel: the root node, its subsurfaces, and its popups and transients as separate nodes. All node state delivered since the previous done event applies atomically at the next done event.
After a denied event the tree, its nodes, and its pacing and input objects are inert: requests on them are ignored except the destructors, and no further events referencing them will be sent — with one deliberate exception: zspatial_exported_buffer_v1 objects are NOT inert after denied. Outstanding buffer releases remain valid and required, so that revocation never strands the producer's client buffers behind unreturnable leases.

entry.name: pacing_exists
entry.summary: the tree already has a pacing object

entry.name: input_exists
entry.summary: the tree already has an input object

entry.name: invalid_bounds
entry.summary: bounds width or height not positive

entry.name: invalid_size
entry.summary: size request width or height not positive

enum.name: denied_reason

description.summary: why an export was refused or revoked

enum.description: The typed reason an export was refused, or a live delegation revoked. policy: producer policy (never detailed further, to avoid oracle probing). protected_content: the content is protected. device_mismatch: the consumer cannot import from the buffer device. session_locked: the producer session locked. no_active_move: a detach_drag found no interactive move. gone: the toplevel was closed or the handle was already inert. gpu_reset: the producer lost the device. unsupported: a required capability is absent or was lost. overrun: the consumer exceeded the advertised in-flight limit — the consumer caused this and may re-export with tighter buffer discipline.

entry.name: resume_move
entry.summary: continue the producer's interactive move at the landing point

request.name: destroy
request.description: Stop the delegation. All node, pacing, and input objects become inert. The producer must cancel outstanding input state it created on behalf of this consumer and must release client buffers only after all outstanding consumer release points have signalled or the consumer connection is gone.

request.name: adopt
request.description:
End the delegation, handing the toplevel back to the producer's window-management authority with a landing hint: a producer output, coordinates in that output's logical coordinate space, and optionally the resume_move flag. The producer places the toplevel at the hint; with resume_move it additionally warps its pointer to the landing point and starts an interactive move there that follows the producer's own pointer motion and ends on the producer's next button-release or cancel, exactly as a move started by xdg_toplevel.move would. If the output is null, was removed, or the hint is otherwise unusable, the producer places the toplevel as if no hint had been given. On an inert (denied) tree, adopt behaves as destroy: the hint is ignored, since the producer already reclaimed the toplevel at revocation.
Only delegated toplevels can be adopted; a consumer-native client can never enter the producer's session, since its connection belongs to the consumer. Object lifetime follows destroy: node, pacing, and input objects become inert and buffer teardown follows the destroy rules.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: the producer output to land on, or null for no hint

arg.name: x
arg.summary: landing x in the output's logical space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: landing y in the output's logical space

request.name: set_bounds
request.description: Communicate the rectangle, in the root node's surface-local coordinate space, available for popup and transient placement. The producer runs its positioner logic (including reconstraint) against these bounds in place of any output-derived work area: the consumer owns the available volume, the producer owns shell placement. The serial is echoed in the configure_bounds event of placements that used it. Width and height must be positive, otherwise the invalid_bounds error is raised.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: consumer serial for this bounds update

arg.name: x
arg.summary: bounds x in root surface-local space

arg.name: y
arg.summary: bounds y in root surface-local space

request.name: request_size

description.summary: ask the producer to resize the toplevel

request.description: Ask the producer to resize the delegated toplevel to the given size in surface-local coordinates. The producer may honor the request through its normal configure path — the result, if any, arrives as ordinary committed state; the producer remains free to constrain or ignore the request per its own rules. While a toplevel is delegated, this request is the only geometry intent the producer should derive configure sizes from; local work-area and output-topology changes must not resize a delegated toplevel. Width and height must be positive, otherwise the invalid_size error is raised.

request.name: set_preferred_scale
request.description: Communicate the scale at which the consumer samples the tree, as a numerator of a base of 120 (the wp-fractional-scale model: 180 means 1.5). The producer should forward it to the delegated client through its normal scale machinery (preferred_buffer_scale or fractional-scale). Consumers must nonetheless handle buffers at any scale the client commits. A value of zero raises the invalid_scale error. If never sent, the producer keeps its own scale choice.

request.name: close

description.summary: ask the producer to close the toplevel

request.description: Ask the producer to close the delegated toplevel through its normal close path (as if the user closed it in the producer's own shell). The client may ignore it; an actual close arrives as unmapped + denied(gone).

request.name: import_timeline
request.description: Import a DRM syncobj timeline for use in attach events and release requests on this tree's buffers. Timelines are imported once and referenced by object thereafter, following the wp-linux-drm-syncobj-v1 model; the fd is consumed by this request.

request.name: get_pacing
request.description: Create the pacing object for this tree. A tree has at most one; a second request raises the pacing_exists error. Without the pacing capability the returned object is inert and the tree receives denied with the unsupported reason.

request.name: get_input
request.description: Create the input back-path object for this tree, bound to the given producer seat: all input delivered through it enters that seat's event streams. A tree has at most one; a second request raises the input_exists error. Without the input capability the returned object is inert and the tree receives denied with the unsupported reason.

arg.name: seat
arg.summary: the producer seat input is delivered on

event.name: anchor
event.description: Sent once, before the first done event, on trees created by detach_drag: the root-surface-local position that was under the producer's cursor at handoff, for grab continuity on the consumer side. Never sent on trees created by export_toplevel.

event.name: flow_control

description.summary: the in-flight limit for this tree

event.description: The maximum number of attaches the consumer may hold unreleased across this tree's buffers. Sent before the first done event and whenever the limit changes. Exceeding it revokes the tree with denied(overrun).

event.name: node
event.description:
Announces a new node of the exported tree and its parent and stacking relation. Nodes are announced parent-first, and within one parent bottom-to-top, so placed_above always references an already-announced sibling (null means bottom-most among current siblings). Restacking of existing nodes is conveyed by the restacked event, never by re-announcing a node. The node's state arrives through events on the node object and applies at the next done event.
If the consumer destroys a node while events referencing it are in flight, subsequent tree events may still reference it; consumers must ignore events referencing nodes they have destroyed.

arg.name: parent
arg.summary: parent node, null for the root

arg.name: placed_above
arg.summary: sibling this node stacks directly above, null for bottom-most

event.name: restacked

description.summary: an existing node changed stacking position

event.description: The node now stacks directly above the given sibling (null for bottom-most among current siblings). Applies at the next done event.

arg.name: placed_above
arg.summary: sibling the node stacks directly above, null for bottom-most

event.name: configure_bounds

description.summary: a placement consumed a bounds update

event.description: The producer placed or reconstrained a popup against the bounds identified by the echoed serial. Lets the consumer correlate popup geometry changes with its own bounds updates.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: the set_bounds serial that was used

event.name: denied
event.description: The export was refused, or a live delegation revoked. The tree and its node, pacing, and input objects are inert from this event on; buffer objects are NOT inert (see the interface description) and their outstanding releases remain required. The producer has already cancelled consumer-originated input state and reclaims local presentation of the toplevel; it releases client buffers only once its own and the consumer's outstanding fenced work completes.

event.name: done
event.description: All node state (buffers, damage, geometry, regions, stacking) delivered since the previous done event applies atomically now. This allows changes to the tree to be seen as atomic, even if they happen via multiple events. The commit id identifies this state for pacing reports; ids increase monotonically per tree and wrap — consumers and producers compare ids by wrapping distance.

interface.name: zspatial_exported_node_v1

description.summary: one surface in the exported tree

interface.description:
One surface of the exported tree, mirroring the client's commits. Buffers are announced as zspatial_exported_buffer_v1 objects and attached by reference; all state applies at the tree's next done event.
When the underlying surface is unmapped or the tree becomes inert, the node is inert: requests other than the destructor are ignored and no further events reference it.

enum.name: fallback_kind
enum.description: Delegated zero-copy delivery is unavailable for this node. shm_only: the client commits wl_shm buffers. device_mismatch: the consumer cannot import from this buffer's device. protected_content: the buffer is protected. color_state: the surface carries committed colour state that version 1 cannot express, and the producer will not deliver silently-misinterpreted pixels. Consumers are expected to present such nodes through a capture-based profile instead; this protocol never falls back to silent copies.

enum.name: decoration_mode
enum.description: client: decorations, if any, are part of the client's buffer (CSD). server_excluded: the producer decorates this window itself and its decoration is NOT part of the exported content — the exported window-geometry excludes it, and the consumer is expected to draw its own affordances (close via zspatial_exported_tree_v1.close, move/resize via its own presentation and request_size).

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the node object. Buffer objects announced through it are not affected; their leases end through their own release and retired semantics.

event.name: buffer
event.description: A buffer entered the node's active set: the client's original allocation, leased to the consumer for sampling. Format is a DRM fourcc; the modifier is hi/lo combined. Plane events follow on the buffer object, one per plane; the plane fds are duplicates owned by the consumer.

arg.name: modifier_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the format modifier

arg.name: modifier_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the format modifier

event.name: attach

description.summary: buffer attached for the next done, with acquire point

event.description: The named buffer is the node's content from the next done event on. The consumer must not sample the buffer before the given point on the given imported timeline signals. Each attach obligates the consumer to exactly one release on the buffer object once its reads complete.

arg.name: point_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the acquire point

arg.name: point_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the acquire point

event.name: damage

description.summary: damage since the previous attach of this buffer

event.description: One damage rectangle in buffer coordinates; sent zero or more times before the done event that applies the attach.

event.name: position
event.description: The node's offset in its parent's surface-local coordinate space. For the root node this event is never sent; the consumer owns the root's placement.

event.name: scale
event.description: The client's buffer scale and output transform for this surface, with transform values as in wl_output.transform.

event.name: viewport
event.description: The surface's wp_viewport state: source rectangle in buffer coordinates (all -1 if unset) and destination size in surface-local coordinates (both -1 if unset).

event.name: geometry
event.description: The xdg-surface window geometry of this node in surface-local coordinates: the part of the surface the consumer should treat as the window, excluding client-side shadows.

event.name: decoration
event.description: How this node is decorated. Sent before the first done event that maps the node, and again on change.

event.name: region_rect

description.summary: one rectangle of a pending region

event.description: One rectangle, surface-local, of the region being replaced; the rectangles accumulate until region_done and replace the previous region of that kind at the next done event.

description.summary: the pending region of this kind is complete

event.name: fallback
event.description: Zero-copy delivery is not available for this node, for the given typed reason. No buffer or attach events will be sent for it.

event.name: unmapped
event.description: The underlying surface was unmapped. The node is inert; outstanding buffer leases still require their releases.

interface.name: zspatial_export_timeline_v1
interface.description: A DRM syncobj timeline imported once and referenced by attach events and release requests, following the wp-linux-drm-syncobj-v1 model of import-once, reference-by-point.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the timeline object. Points already communicated remain valid; the underlying syncobj lives until both sides drop it.

interface.name: zspatial_exported_buffer_v1
interface.description:
One client buffer leased to the consumer. Plane events describe the dmabuf; each attach on the owning node obligates exactly one release. The producer joins the consumer's release point with its own completion before releasing the buffer to its client; the consumer never touches the client's release timeline. Releases may complete out of order across buffers.
Buffer objects are exempt from tree inertness on denied: releases and destruction remain valid after revocation, so leases always unwind.

entry.name: excess_release
entry.summary: release sent without a matching outstanding attach

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the buffer object. If attaches are outstanding, the producer must treat the lease as ended only when the consumer connection's outstanding release points signal or the connection is gone; a consumer should send its releases before destroying the object.

request.name: release
request.description: Return one outstanding attach of this buffer: the consumer signals the given point on the given imported timeline when its reads of the buffer complete. Sending more releases than there are outstanding attaches raises the excess_release error.

arg.name: point_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of the release point

arg.name: point_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of the release point

event.name: plane
event.description: One plane of the buffer, in plane-index order; num_planes such events follow the announcing buffer event. The fd is a duplicate owned by the consumer.

event.name: retired
event.description: The client freed or replaced this buffer; it will not be attached again. The object is inert once all outstanding attaches are released; the consumer should then destroy it.

interface.name: zspatial_export_pacing_v1
interface.description:
Consumer-driven pacing for one exported tree. While this object exists and a clock has been set, the producer dispatches the tree's client frame callbacks against the consumer's cadence instead of its own outputs'; destroying the object atomically returns the tree to producer-paced mode. Exactly one pacing mode owns a tree at any time.
The consumer reports presentation outcomes through mark_presented and mark_discarded; the producer translates them into its own presentation-time feedback toward the delegated client. Exactly one of the two must be reported for every done commit id while consumer-paced.

entry.name: invalid_clock
entry.summary: the clock id is not a supported CLOCK_* value

enum.name: presented_flags
enum.description: zero_copy means the consumer scanned out or sampled the client's buffer directly in its final presentation path. It must never be set merely because no intermediate allocation existed on the wire.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: return the tree to producer pacing

request.description: Destroy the pacing object. The tree atomically returns to producer-paced frame callback dispatch. Outcome reports for commits already made are no longer possible; the producer resolves their client feedback by its own rules.

request.name: set_consumer_clock
request.description: Supply the consumer's presentation clock (a CLOCK_* id valid for clock_gettime; an unsupported id raises the invalid_clock error) and correlation to the producer's CLOCK_MONOTONIC: a pair of timestamps sampled together, so the producer can convert frame arguments into its own domain. Clocks drift: consumers should resend the correlation periodically (once per second is sufficient for millisecond-accurate cutoffs).

request.name: frame
request.description: One upcoming consumer frame: predicted display time (consumer clock, nanoseconds, hi/lo), the frame period, and the commit cutoff before display time by which tree state must be done to be sampled. The producer schedules the tree's client frame callbacks so commits land before the cutoff. Sending frame before set_consumer_clock raises the no_clock error.

arg.name: display_time_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of predicted display ns

arg.name: display_time_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of predicted display ns

arg.name: cutoff_ns
arg.summary: commit cutoff before display time, ns

request.name: mark_presented

description.summary: report that a commit was first sampled

request.description: Report that the consumer first sampled the tree state identified by commit_id at the given time (consumer clock, nanoseconds, hi/lo). The producer translates this into presentation feedback toward its client.

arg.name: time_hi
arg.summary: upper 32 bits of sample time ns

arg.name: time_lo
arg.summary: lower 32 bits of sample time ns

request.name: mark_discarded

description.summary: report that a commit was never sampled

request.description: Report that the tree state identified by commit_id was never sampled — a newer state replaced it first, or it missed its cutoff and the consumer reused the last ready state.

interface.name: zspatial_export_input_v1
interface.description:
The input back-path for one exported tree, bound to one producer seat. Requests address tree nodes in surface-local coordinates; the producer translates them into its own protocol streams towards its client, generating its own wire serials and owning implicit grabs, popup dismissal, and focus. Requests naming an inert node are ignored. Drag-and-drop is absent in version 1; producers advertise it with the dnd capability when a future version adds it.
The bound seat is shared with the producer's local session: this protocol assumes one human using both presentations, and consumer input contends for seat focus like any local interaction. Delivering consumer keyboard input moves the producer's keyboard focus to the delegated surface; keyboard_enter and keyboard_leave carry the consumer's focus intent so the producer can apply its own focus policy.
Pointer and touch requests accumulate and are delivered to the producer's client at the frame requests, following wl_pointer and wl_touch frame semantics. The time argument is advisory ordering information in milliseconds; producers must restamp events into their own clock domain on delivery (using the pacing clock correlation when available), so inter-event timing the client observes is always producer-clock-consistent.

request.name: destroy
request.description: Destroy the input object. The producer cancels consumer-originated pointer, keyboard, and touch state towards its client (pointer leave, key releases, touch cancel).

request.name: pointer_leave

description.summary: the consumer's pointer left the tree

request.description: The consumer's cursor or ray left the exported tree. The producer delivers pointer leave to its client and clears consumer-originated hover state, subject to its own grab rules (an implicit grab continues until its buttons release).

request.name: pointer_button
request.description: Button codes and state values follow wl_pointer.button semantics.

request.name: pointer_axis
request.description: Axis values follow wl_pointer.axis semantics; high-resolution discrete steps accompany as pointer_axis_value120 within the same frame.

request.name: pointer_axis_value120
request.description: Discrete axis movement in fractions of 120, following wl_pointer.axis_value120 semantics.

description.summary: end of a logical pointer event group

request.name: keyboard_enter

description.summary: the consumer focused the tree for keyboard input

request.description: The consumer's user directed keyboard focus at the given node. The producer applies its own focus policy; if it grants focus, its seat keyboard focus moves to the delegated surface.

request.name: keyboard_leave

description.summary: the consumer's keyboard focus left the tree

request.description: The producer releases consumer-originated keyboard focus (delivering key releases for keys this object pressed) and restores its own focus policy.

request.name: keyboard_key
request.description: Key codes are in the keymap announced by the keymap event whose serial is given; keys sent with a stale serial after a keymap change are dropped by the producer (never reinterpreted in the wrong map). The producer computes and delivers modifier state to its client itself.

arg.name: keymap_serial
arg.summary: serial of the keymap the code is valid in

arg.name: key
arg.summary: key code in the announced keymap

request.name: keyboard_keysym
request.description: A key event expressed as an xkb keysym instead of a keycode, for consumers whose users type on layouts the producer's keymap cannot be assumed to contain. The producer maps the keysym into its delivery machinery itself (which may involve temporary keymap amendment); state follows wl_keyboard.key_state. Consumers should prefer keyboard_key when they can produce valid codes.

description.summary: touch point down on a node

request.name: touch_cancel
request.description: The consumer took over the touch sequence for its own gestures (or lost its input source). The producer delivers wl_touch.cancel to its client for the sequence this object forwarded.

description.summary: end of a logical touch event group

request.name: activate
request.description: The consumer's user performed an activating gesture on the node. This never carries a foreign xdg-activation token: the producer mints and validates its own token from this intent, subject to its focus-stealing policy.

entry.name: pointer_grab
entry.summary: an implicit or popup pointer grab

event.name: keymap

description.summary: the keymap key codes are interpreted in

event.description: The keymap the producer's client receives; keyboard_key codes must be valid in it and must carry this event's serial. Sent before the first keyboard_key may be sent, and again with a new serial whenever the producer's keymap changes. The fd is a duplicate owned by the consumer.

event.name: focus
event.description: Reports where the producer's focus or an active grab of the given kind sits within this tree, or null when it left the tree. Purely informational: the producer owns the state.

event.name: popup_dismissed
event.description: The producer broke a popup grab (for example on an outside click it synthesized, or its own policy). The consumer should stop presenting the node; the unmapped event on the node follows.
